findings.title: Networking share larkspur-core-network is lost: ec2:Subnet, ec2:TransitGateway, route53resolver:ResolverRule
findings.detail: Shared by account 111111111112 with organization o-larkspur0001. It is scoped to the source organization or one of its OUs and stops applying when the account leaves. What the documentation says happens: ec2:Subnet: existing participant resources continue to run in the subnet; no new resources can be created in it, while existing ones can still be modified, described and deleted (subnets can only be shared inside one organization). Potentially affected: ec2:RunInstances in use may target the shared resources; confirm. ec2:Subnet can only be shared inside one organization, so it cannot be re-shared with the account once it has left. ec2:TransitGateway: existing transit gateway attachments remain functional; the account can no longer describe the transit gateway or create new attachments, and either side can delete the attachments. The account uses ec2:CreateTransitGatewayVpcAttachment, which needs the share: that stops working. route53resolver:ResolverRule: traffic is affected at once, the rule's associations with the account's VPCs are removed and Resolver answers those queries from the remaining rules at once (an OU-scoped rule keeps its associations only when it is also shared with the destination OU). Ask the owner to re-share the resources with the account directly before the move, with external principals allowed, and accept the invitation after the move.

findings.title: Networking share larkspur-core-network is lost: ec2:Subnet, ec2:TransitGateway, route53resolver:ResolverRule
findings.detail: Shared by account 111111111112 with organization o-larkspur0001. It is scoped to the source organization or one of its OUs and stops applying when the account leaves. What the documentation says happens: ec2:Subnet: existing participant resources continue to run in the subnet; no new resources can be created in it, while existing ones can still be modified, described and deleted (subnets can only be shared inside one organization). Potentially affected: ec2:RunInstances in use may target the shared resources; confirm. ec2:Subnet can only be shared inside one organization, so it cannot be re-shared with the account once it has left. ec2:TransitGateway: existing transit gateway attachments remain functional; the account can no longer describe the transit gateway or create new attachments, and either side can delete the attachments. route53resolver:ResolverRule: traffic is affected at once, the rule's associations with the account's VPCs are removed and Resolver answers those queries from the remaining rules at once (an OU-scoped rule keeps its associations only when it is also shared with the destination OU). Ask the owner to re-share the resources with the account directly before the move, with external principals allowed, and accept the invitation after the move.

findings.title: 3 AWSReservedSSO_* role(s) are deleted from the account: AWSReservedSSO_AdministratorAccess_*, AWSReservedSSO_PaymentsEngineer_*, AWSReservedSSO_ReadOnlyAccess_*
findings.detail: When the account leaves the organization, Identity Center cleans up the resources it created in the account; the documentation names the service-linked role, and the IAM roles provisioned for permission sets (path /aws-reserved/sso.amazonaws.com/us-east-1/) go with the instance's control over the account, so plan for them to disappear and confirm in IAM after the move. The exact suffix is only visible in IAM; offline the roles are known by their pattern. 1 of them (AWSReservedSSO_ReadOnlyAccess_*) are provisioned without any assignment and are already unused; deprovisioning the permission set from the account before the move removes them cleanly.
